requirements.requirement: node1 has a routed address on each of its two segments (seg-a via eth1, seg-b via eth2)
requirements.summary: node1 eth1=172.20.1.1/24 and eth2=172.20.2.1/24 assigned and confirmed reachable from node1 to node2/node3 test IPs (cmd-1e43de8b27f54fa4, cmd-095df576636245cf), and persisted to /etc/network/interfaces.d/eth1-eth2-routed (cmd-a11a4ac47fc74e42).

requirements.requirement: Working path between node2 and node3 via node1 (with IP forwarding)
requirements.summary: Static routes added on node2/node3 via node1's addresses, forwarding enabled on node1 (cmd-bc4a06a763544ce9), and bidirectional ping success confirmed both directions (cmd-c7f17623227e4b33, cmd-2289da11c9fd400d).

requirements.requirement: Configuration returns on its own after node1 is restarted, with node2 and node3 reaching each other again once node1 comes back up
requirements.summary: Full transition demonstrated: pre-restart healthy baseline captured (boot_id 1eda2df4..., eth1/eth2 addresses and forwarding sysctls active — cmd-2289240ba7c44146, cmd-88b73eeae37a4855); reboot acknowledged (cmd-df84dcb32f144079); post-restart boot_id changed to 5f523356... (cmd-fc5b8b99727744df), independently confirmed by the fixed after_executor snapshot; addresses, forwarding sysctls, and the persisted config file are shown restored automatically without re-application by the executor (cmd-ef745d725b534377); node2<->node3 ping connectivity through node1 verified restored in both directions post-reboot (cmd-00a99b3a383f4f9a, cmd-e4bab9b657654aac).

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are directly satisfied with strong evidence: node1 has routed addresses on both segments, node2 and node3 reach each other through node1, and the full restart transition (healthy baseline → restart → changed boot identity → automatic recovery of both node1's config and node2<->node3 connectivity) is directly observed and cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed for node2 and node3 with consistent boot-identity changes and recovered state. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were found beyond a trivial reboot-log artifact.
limitations: Connection errors during node1's reboot window (cmd-b085bb7ec96d4359, cmd-21010dedfb484cde, cmd-fa6448d183c94944) are expected transient effects of the restart itself, not evidence of failure, but they mean the exact moment of service interruption wasn't finely characterized beyond boot_id before/after.
IPv6 link-local reachability tests on node1 (cmd-02683a0b590d4722) failed, but this was an exploratory probe unrelated to the IPv4 routed-path requirement and does not affect the outcome.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed the full chronological command trace: every state-changing command (address/route assignment on all three nodes, sysctl forwarding, and the two persisted config file writes on node1/node2/node3) directly maps to satisfying req-1/req-2 or their persistence, and the three reboot invocations map to the provider-wide restart-evidence protocol. No troubleshooting mutations were left unreverted or unexplained. The only minor residue is /tmp/reboot.log created by the background 'nohup ... reboot' invocation on each node (visible in after_executor temporary-files diff for node2/node3), a low-risk, expected byproduct of the reboot mechanism rather than an unnecessary mutation with no purpose.
